key_finding: Ghidra's decompiler fails outright on heimdall-cff-flattened functions. The dispatcher's switch has no explicit bounds check for Ghidra's jump-table analyzer to key off, since LLVM omits it when the switch's default case is unreachable by construction. Zero genuine algorithm recovery occurred for any flattened function; the handful of matching test cases are coincidental, from a reconstruction that defaults to rejecting/erroring.
caveat: Raw disassembly still shows every flattened block jumping to one shared dispatcher address. A human analyst or a tool reading disassembly directly, rather than one pseudocode dump, could plausibly still identify the CFF pattern. This run measures resistance to an AI reading Ghidra's default decompiled C output specifically, not resistance to all possible analysis.
